title: Rabbi Yoshiyah of Usha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: It is very likely that he was Babylonian and studied there under Rav and Shmuel. In [Menachot 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.39a.6), Rabba bar bar Chana introduces the teaching with “Rabbi Yoshiyah of Usha told me.” Hyman adds that Yoshiyah was speaking in Shmuel’s name.[^2] The Rabbi Yoshiyah who reports a teaching in Rav’s name in [Sukkah 2b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.2b.5) appears to be this Rabbi Yoshiyah of Usha.

He subsequently went up to the Land of Israel and became the leading authority at Usha. In [Gittin 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.33b.12), Rabba bar bar Chana says: “We were five elders before Rabbi Yoshiyah of Usha.” In [Bekhorot 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.28b.4), he says to Rabba bar bar Chana: “Come, and I will show you films on the eye that change.”[^1]

Were I not afraid to venture the suggestion, I would say that the text in [Berakhot 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.22a.25-22b.1), “When Ravin came, he said: An incident occurred at Usha, in the entrance hall of Rav Oshaya,” should read “of Rabbi Yoshiyah.” The matter requires further examination.

notes.text: Hyman cites Sukkah 20b; the teaching is at 2b:5. His בהקין corresponds to the Bavli’s בדוקין, films or opacities of the eye. ריש means ‘head’ or ‘leading authority,’ without specifying a formal office.

In [Menachot 39a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.39a.6), Rav Yosef says that Shmuel gave the ruling that Rabbah had attributed to Rav. Rabba bar bar Chana then quotes Yoshiyah giving the same ruling without naming Yoshiyah’s source. At [Berakhot 22a–22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.22a.25-22b.1), the text reads “Rav Oshaya’s chamber,” the reading Hyman proposes to change.
